To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of organoselenium compounds are dependent on the chemical structure and that p‐XSC, p‐XMS and SM, but not MSC, inhibit cell growth in LNCaP prostate cancer cells and that the effects on cell growth are associated with inhibition of PSA secretion and changes in the expression of genes that regulate cell proliferation.
the effects of organoselenium compounds are dependent on the structure and the cell type.

(i) p‐XSC, a synthetic organoselenium compound, inhibits growth of human prostate cancer cell lines and reduces levels of PSA in the medium, (ii) p‐XCS induces oxidative stress in human prostate cancer cell line and (iii) p‐XSE increases p53 expression in androgen responsive human prostate cancer cell but not in androgen independent human cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and development of new chemopreventative agents against cancer.
the identification and characterization of novel organoselenium chemopreventives and their mechanism of action in prostate cancer cells.
the development and characterization of new organoselenium compounds that are effective in the treatment of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
selenium supplementation is not only beneficial to the prostate but is also beneficial to the whole body and is an essential trace mineral.
p‐XSC is a more potent agent than the other three organoselenium compounds tested.
the effects of organoselenium compounds are cell‐specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the organoselenium compounds, p‐XMS, p‐XCS and SM, but not MSC, inhibited growth of androgen‐responsive human prostate carcinoma LNCaP, but not androgen‐independent human prostate carcinoma Lncap C‐4‐2 cells.
the effects of organoselenium compounds depend on the chemical structure and the cellular context.
the synthetic compounds p‐XMS and p‐XSS are more efficacious than SM and MSC in inhibiting growth of prostate cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organoselenium compounds can be developed as chemoprevention agents in prostate cancer.
the effects of different forms of selenium on prostate cancer cells are very different.
the effects of organoselenium compounds are highly dependent on their chemical structures.
